newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares climb on back of SKB's gains.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares climb on back of SKB's gains.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped 3.53 percent on Friday after spectacular gains in the shares of bank SKB. But traders said the market would likely come under correction next week after today's steep rise.

"SKB was obviously pushed up by news that there's been strong demand for its global depository receipts abroad -- the share price could grow over 90,000 tolars," Karmen Korbun, a trader at bank Creditanstalt said.
Bank SKB said earlier that its GDR issue abroad was 25 times oversubscribed.
The 10-share SBI index rose 53.65 points to 1,573.6. The index has risen 36 percent since the beginning of the year mainly on the back of foreign buying.
Overall nine shares rose, seven fell and nine were untraded. Turnover almost tripled to 1.2 billion tolars from 429.8 million.
Bank SKB was the most active and the biggest gainer, jumping 25.62 percent to 73,800 tolars on volume of 13,687 shares for total turnover of one billion tolars.
Demand for SKB has increased significantly due to the bank's plan to list global depository receipts on the London Stock Exchange in the middle of February.
Last week the Bank of Slovenia gave its accord to SKB's listing abroad by giving the green light to increase the maximum foreign shareholding in SKB to 49 percent from 30 percent.
Brokerage Nika led the day's decliners, falling 7.74 percent to 4,050 tolars on volume of 68 shares.
